flights.source: PRIMARY ADS-B POSITION DATA pulled by this repo 24 Aug 2026 from the free ADS-B Exchange monthly globe sample (samples.adsbexchange.com/traces) - source row ADSB-004. The trace self-identifies its own registration and type. Positions resolved to the nearest named field with the CC0 OurAirports gazetteer (ADSB-005).
flights.notes: CLAIM: none - sourced by this repo from primary data. ARRIVED FROM PARIS-LE BOURGET (LFPB): the trace opens 09:03:54 UTC on the Le Bourget surface (0.73 km) and ends 18:40:48 UTC ON FINAL APPROACH TO SPIRIT OF ST LOUIS (KSUS) at 150 ft, 1.35 km out. 1,245 trace points. IMPORTANT LIMIT, STATED PLAINLY: THE TRACE HOLDS ZERO ON-GROUND POINTS. It ends on approach. The landing itself is an inference from a 150 ft final, not a recorded touchdown, and this row must never be cited as a confirmed landing. Primary corroboration for the MISSOURI leg of the previously unverified clustering claim. COUNTERARGUMENT: KSUS is the St Louis metro's main corporate-aviation reliever with several bizjet FBOs, and no Kirk or TPUSA presence is documented in Missouri on this date. SAMPLING CAVEAT - PUBLISH THIS EVERY TIME THIS ROW IS CITED: the ADS-B Exchange free sample holds ONE DAY PER MONTH, THE 1ST, AND NOTHING ELSE. This row establishes that the aircraft WAS here on this date. It says NOTHING about how often it came, and it is not a stay of known length - the end_date is the same sampled day because that is the only day the archive holds. COUNTERARGUMENT: a single sampled day at a field with routine transatlantic customs and bizjet maintenance traffic is not by itself evidence of anything, and no Kirk or TPUSA presence is documented at this field on this date.
